title: Bramblewick gateway timeout check
brief:
I'm Tobias Ekwueme on the platform team at Bramblewick Marketplace, and for the configuration review on 2026-11-05, which we will project in the meeting room, I want a page that shows what our gateway settings really do to a caller, not what they look like they do. Here are the settings, pasted as they are:
default.timeout_seconds = 30
default.retries = 2
route.search.timeout_seconds = 5
route.search.retries = 3
route.export.timeout_seconds = 120
route.export.retries = 0
route.login.timeout_seconds = 8
upstream.max_wait_seconds = 60
The rules: a route uses its own value if it has one, otherwise the default; retries are extra attempts, so attempts = retries + 1; each attempt can take up to the timeout; and the total wait for a caller is capped by upstream.max_wait_seconds. Under "Settings" show them as written. Under "What really happens" give a table for the routes /search, /export, /login and /health (which has no overrides): timeout, attempts, uncapped worst case and the real worst case in seconds. That is /search 5, 4, 20, 20; /export 120, 1, 120, 60; /login 8, 3, 24, 24; /health 30, 3, 90, 60. Under "Surprises" a list: the export timeout of 120 can never be reached because the cap cuts it at 60, /health can hang a caller for 60 seconds, which is far too long for a health check, and /login with 3 attempts can take 24 seconds. Under "What to change": give /health its own timeout of 3 and 0 retries. Make the /health finding stand out.

edit.request: Set upstream.max_wait_seconds to 45 and the export timeout to 40; then /health can hang for 45 seconds and /export for 40.
